topic: Are there any particles that behave oppositely to the properties or states of photons?
reframed_question: Can an operation-resolved quantum-state ledger distinguish photon self-conjugacy from measurable opposite helicity, propagation, polarization, or structured-mode states?
discipline: quantum field theory and quantum optics
principal_conclusion: The photon is its own antiparticle in the standard description. Contrasting helicity, polarization, momentum direction, and OAM labels denote states of the same photon species, so each alleged opposite must be specified by a symmetry operation and observable.
